Process

Four short breakdowns of how a scene actually gets built — the problem, the approach, and what it cost.

The shape of a job

  1. 01

    Work out what the film is

    Before anything gets made, one sentence has to hold: what happens, and to whom. If it does not survive being said out loud, no amount of craft rescues it later.

  2. 02

    Find the look

    Reference first, then a small set of rules — palette, lens, how light behaves in this world. Fixing that early is what stops a sequence drifting apart in the middle.

  3. 03

    Build the sequence

    Shot by shot, in order, held against continuity: the same face, the same room, the same time of day. This is the slow part, and it is where most of the work goes.

  4. 04

    Cut, grade, finish

    The edit decides the rhythm — where it breathes and where it moves. Then sound, then grade, then delivery in the format the film is actually going to be watched in.
